prompt: automake parallel make recovery locking portable test-and-set command
answer:
Use `mkdir` as the portable filesystem-level test-and-set operation:

```sh
if mkdir data.lock 2>/dev/null; then
    # First process: owns the lock
    rm -f data.stamp
    $(MAKE) $(AM_MAKEFLAGS) data.stamp
    result=$?
    rm -rf data.lock
    exit $result
else
    # Follower processes: wait for the lock owner
    while test -d data.lock; do
        sleep 1
    done
    test -f data.stamp
fi
```

In an Automake recovery rule, add a trap to remove the lock on interruption:

```make
data.c data.h data.w data.x: data.stamp
	@if test -f $@; then :; else \
	  trap 'rm -rf data.lock data.stamp' 1 2 13 15; \
	  if mkdir data.lock 2>/dev/null; then \
	    rm -f data.stamp; \
	    $(MAKE) $(AM_MAKEFLAGS) data.stamp; \
	    result=$$?; rm -rf data.lock; exit $$result; \
	  else \
	    while test -d data.lock; do sleep 1; done; \
	    test -f data.stamp; \
	  fi; \
	fi
```

The Automake documentation describes `mkdir` as a portable test-and-set mechanism for this purpose.
